findings.title: Added time.sleep(0.1) is a no-op because the test monkeypatches time.sleep
findings.body: The test calls `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)` at the top, so the `time.sleep(0.1)` added here is also a no-op. The comment says it gives flusher threads time to process after the drift change, but it gives them no time. `step.join()` then races the flusher thread, so `messages` may be empty and `(msg,) = messages` fails intermittently. The added `step.poll()` does not fix this. Use a real wait (e.g. poll until messages appear with a deadline) or restore the real sleep for this wait.

findings.title: --flusher-processes defaults to 1, contradicting the one-process-per-shard design
findings.body: The PR says the flusher should spawn a process per redis shard, and SpanFlusher treats a None `max_processes` as one process per assigned shard. But the CLI option defaults to 1, so production consumers that don't pass the flag get a single flusher process for all shards. The help text ('Defaults to 1') also describes behavior that differs from the factory/flusher default. Either default to None (per-shard) or update the PR's intent and the help text to match.

findings.title: New parameter inserted before produce_to_pipe changes positional argument meaning
findings.body: `flusher_processes` was inserted between `output_block_size` and `produce_to_pipe`. Any caller passing `produce_to_pipe` positionally now binds it to `flusher_processes`, which silently changes behavior (an int/callable mismatch that may not fail immediately). Add the new parameter after `produce_to_pipe` or make the rest keyword-only.

findings.title: Restart of a hung thread-based flusher starts a second flusher on the same shards
findings.body: In `_ensure_processes_alive`, the old process is only killed when it is a `multiprocessing.Process`. For threads (the `produce_to_pipe` path), the old thread is left running and `_create_process_for_shards` starts a new thread on the same shards. Two flushers can then concurrently flush the same shard buffer. The previous code would have failed loudly here; now it silently duplicates work. Either refuse to restart threads or make the old one stop before starting the new one.

findings.title: Unused _create_process_for_shard method
findings.body: `_create_process_for_shard` (singular) is never called; restarts go through `_ensure_processes_alive`, which calls `_create_process_for_shards` directly. It is dead code that also duplicates the shard-to-process lookup, so it should be removed or used.

findings.title: Inconsistent metric tag key: 'shard' vs 'shards'
findings.body: The `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` and `segment_size_bytes` metrics use the tag key `shard`, while `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` uses `shards` for the same value. Dashboards and alerts filtering on one key will miss the other timer, so the tag should be consistent.

findings.title: test_flusher_processes_limit does not verify any flushing output
findings.body: The test is named for the process limit but only checks counts and shard distribution, then calls `join()`. It never submits spans or checks that flushed segments reach the produce pipe for every shard. A regression that drops a shard's segments would still pass.
